source: BHPC manual and repo methodology taxonomy

frameworks.name: Never Miss Twice Continuity Protocol
frameworks.definition: prevents one missed day from becoming identity-level drift

frameworks.name: Minimum Viable Day Recovery Protocol
frameworks.definition: shrinks the day to one meaningful action when capacity is low

frameworks.name: No Catch-Up Closure Rule
frameworks.definition: closes missed work without turning yesterday into punishment

frameworks.name: Daily Agenda Engine
frameworks.definition: turns goals and constraints into a daily execution stack

frameworks.name: Arbitration Engine
frameworks.definition: chooses between competing priorities using leverage, urgency, energy, compounding, and downside

frameworks.name: Three-Chat Architecture
frameworks.definition: separates source-of-truth rules, daily runtime, and governance edits

frameworks.name: Foreground Priority Selection Rule
frameworks.definition: protects one project as the main execution target

frameworks.name: Executive Review Mode
frameworks.definition: organizes known strategy without adding new theories

frameworks.name: High-Pressure Coaching Mode
frameworks.definition: challenges avoidance when comfort language would keep the loop open

frameworks.name: Chief-of-Staff Logic Layer
frameworks.definition: sequences priorities and converts ambiguity into next actions

frameworks.name: Accountability Mirror Protocol
frameworks.definition: compares stated commitments with observable completion evidence

frameworks.name: Ambiguity Stop Rule
frameworks.definition: halts vague tasks until the physical action is named

frameworks.name: First Hour Launch Sequence
frameworks.definition: uses one physical start and one focused work block to break inertia

frameworks.name: Recovery Mode Operating Rule
frameworks.definition: protects continuity without pretending capacity is normal

frameworks.name: End-of-Day Evidence Loop
frameworks.definition: closes the day with completed, partial, and missed evidence

frameworks.name: Billionaire Mindset Track
frameworks.definition: filters opportunities through ownership, leverage, asymmetry, and downside containment

frameworks.name: Continuity Over Intensity Rule
frameworks.definition: prioritizes repeatable participation over heroic effort

frameworks.name: No Mid-Day Renegotiation Rule
frameworks.definition: keeps emotional volatility from rewriting the plan at 2 PM

frameworks.name: Operator Discipline Filter
frameworks.definition: turns discipline into structure instead of self-criticism

frameworks.name: Strategic Patience Filter
frameworks.definition: prevents impulsive pivots before evidence is available

frameworks.name: Prompt Pack Installation Flow
frameworks.definition: turns a normal LLM into a structured operating system

frameworks.name: Decision Fatigue Reduction Protocol
frameworks.definition: reduces unnecessary choices before the day begins

frameworks.name: Execution Evidence Ledger
frameworks.definition: uses observable outcomes instead of intention as the source of truth

frameworks.name: System Drift Recovery Protocol
frameworks.definition: restarts the system without shame analysis or reset theater

frameworks.name: Capacity-Matched Execution Rule
frameworks.definition: fits work to current energy without abandoning the day
